claims.text: A hybrid combination of DSC, in-situ neutron imaging, and third-generation CALPHAD can accurately determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, melting volume change, and liquid thermodynamic properties across the HEA family.
The proposed hybrid method will determine these properties efficiently across HEAs.
The target samples can generally be treated as solid, single-phase HEAs in as-cast or well-equilibrated conditions.
Moderate-to-slow heating rates minimize thermal lag and ensure equilibrium during the measurements.
In-situ neutron imaging can capture liquid-phase homogeneity and the remixing of phase-separated liquids in an HEA.
Local atomic and short-range chemical order in HEAs affects their phase-transition signatures.
DSC can effectively capture local atomic and short-range chemical order in HEAs.
The proposed neutron imaging can effectively capture local atomic and short-range chemical order in HEAs.
A characteristic DSC endothermic peak identifies fusion and provides the fusion thermal signal.
In-situ neutron imaging can verify melting and liquid-phase formation in an HEA.
In-situ neutron imaging can quantitatively determine the volume change at melting.
Third-generation CALPHAD descriptions can reliably represent relevant solid- and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties for HEA applications.
Comparison with CALPHAD calculations incorporating high-entropy effects can deconvolve complex experimental signals into melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, and latent volume change.
The hybrid method is expected to achieve errors of approximately 5–10% for fusion properties.
The hybrid method will be more accurate than traditional single-technique approaches.
Measured liquid-phase thermodynamic properties will be consistent with third-generation CALPHAD predictions across a broad HEA compositional space.
Standalone DSC or indirect thermodynamic estimation in HEAs often has errors greater than 10–15%.
Extreme compositional inhomogeneity or dominant phase separation makes the hybrid approach less applicable.
Limited neutron-imaging resolution at very high temperatures imposes a practical boundary on the approach.
Multicomponent liquid mixing may not conform to available CALPHAD models without additional empirical refinement.
